regime_note: Draft PR #121 delivers a nominal ~100 m grid, aggregating 3x3 source cells before the percentile. The source read is deliberately unchanged, so the composite stage's bytes stand, but its working set, its task count, and its output size all move, and PR #121 gate 4 leaves R_COMPOSITE_MB_S unrevised. Recalibrate against a 100 m run before quoting any figure here after #121 lands.

buckets.measured: A retained artifact in this repository is the observation itself.
buckets.derived: Arithmetic over other quantities, never stronger than its weakest input.
buckets.assumed: A modelling choice, carrying a value, a range, and a sensitivity.
buckets.user_reported: Transcribed from an external system with no export retained.
buckets.unknown: Cannot be settled from this repository. Never given a value.

quantities.name: reference_fleet_shape
quantities.unit: (vms, vcpus, cluster minutes, usd/h) per cluster
quantities.source: S30W065 2026-08-23, clusters 1954303 / 1954376 / 1954375, from the Coiled cluster event log exports retained by SHA-256 digest in cluster_records.json
quantities.upgrade: Nothing for the shape itself. The exports carry no instance type for the scheduler each cluster also runs, so that VM-time is counted and left unpriced.

quantities.name: reference_worker_lifetimes
quantities.source: 'Instance starting' to each worker's last event, summing to 1369.3 worker VM-minutes against 1859.5 for vms x cluster lifetime. Five of the recovery round's fourteen workers lived 1.89 minutes and never reached compute
quantities.upgrade: Nothing. It is the billed window the event log records.

quantities.name: reference_scheduler_vm_hours
quantities.source: every cluster runs a scheduler instance beside its workers and the event log times all three. The fleet shape counts workers only, so this VM-time sits outside every figure below
quantities.upgrade: The export gives no instance type for the scheduler, so the model reports this VM-time and declines to price it.

quantities.name: vm_infrastructure_boot_minutes
quantities.source: worst per-cluster median of 'Queued for launch' to 'Successfully phoned home' across the three clusters: 0.75 / 0.92 / 0.83
quantities.upgrade: Nothing, and it does not replace vm_boot_minutes. It stops when dask registers, before the software environment starts and before the first task runs, so it is a component of the 5-minute figure rather than a contradiction of it.

quantities.name: reference_billed_aws_usd
quantities.source: $2.19 + $4.55 + $0.54 spot, spoken; appears in no commit of this repository. The cluster records recovered on 2026-09-02 are Coiled event logs and Coiled billing activity, neither of which carries an AWS dollar figure
quantities.upgrade: Attach the AWS Cost Explorer export or invoice line for 2026-08-23.

quantities.name: reference_billed_credits
quantities.source: Coiled billing activity per cluster, 67.8106 / 16.1450 / 184.1507, retained per cluster in cluster_records.json. The total reproduces the 268.11 quota.py already carried, so what the record changes is the denominator, not this
quantities.upgrade: Nothing. The per-cluster split is the observation.

quantities.name: vm_boot_minutes
quantities.source: budgets.VM_BOOT_S = 300; '4-5 min observed' across the S30W065 runs of 2026-08-21/22
quantities.upgrade: Retain the driver logs those boots were read from, or time a boot in the probe run.

quantities.name: offsets_unit_compute_minutes
quantities.source: ADR-016: offsets-side shards computed for about six minutes each
quantities.upgrade: Publish per-unit start and finish stamps from a shard's own state objects.

quantities.name: composite_fastest_vm_minutes
quantities.source: fastest composite VM finished at 20 min; the fleet's spread was 20-32 min
quantities.upgrade: Publish per-unit timings; the spread to 32 is unattributed between work and wait.

quantities.name: composite_unit_compute_minutes
quantities.source: the fastest VM's wall clock minus one boot, treating the 20-32 spread as straggler and barrier time rather than work
quantities.upgrade: Per-unit timings would make this derived. If half the spread is work, the composite term rises about 40% and it already carries 84% of compute.

quantities.name: spot_fraction_band
quantities.source: pricing.json spot_band, provenance 'assumed'; samples 0.35 / 0.44 / 0.71 on 2026-08-14. Valid because settings.shard_spot_policy is 'spot'; under spot_with_fallback the upper bound is 1.00
quantities.upgrade: Not reducible. Spot is priced per type, per AZ, per minute, and a finished run cannot be repriced against what it paid.

quantities.name: credits_per_vcpu_hour_band
quantities.source: per-cluster credits over per-cluster measured worker vCPU-hours: 0.902 / 0.948 / 1.003. quota.py's 0.6-1.25 ran the same division against vms x cluster lifetime, which charges every worker for the wall clock of the slowest. Its width was the staggered exits, exactly as its own note guessed, and not a varying rate
quantities.upgrade: Nothing from this run. A second billed run would say whether the rate moves between workspaces or over time.

quantities.name: s3_standard_usd_per_gb_month
quantities.source: AWS S3 Standard list price, us-west-2
quantities.upgrade: Nothing. It is a published list price.

quantities.name: output_gb_per_tile
quantities.source: compressed COG pair at the 30 m grid; no shipped tile was measured
quantities.upgrade: Measure a shipped tile. #121 cuts the uncompressed output 9x, so this is one of the inputs that goes stale first. Immaterial either way at ~$24/month.

quantities.name: consolidation_capture_bands
quantities.source: ADR-017: capture = 1 - 1/R for queue depth R. At 700 tiles the first offsets wave buffers about 10,500 units against a 64-VM cap, R about 164, boot capture 0.994. Idle capture is lower because a tail wave, a final round's stragglers, a competing composite stage, and tiles not becoming ready together all remain.
quantities.upgrade: The ~$0.50 queues_surplus probe in ADR-017, then a capped calibration run that counts boots and idle VM-minutes.

quantities.name: queues_surplus_holds
quantities.source: ADR-017 backend contract: read from documented Coiled semantics and never verified against real Coiled by this project
quantities.upgrade: The ~$0.50 one-wave probe: more units than workers, count the workers that start and how units distribute. Until it passes, every capture figure is an assumption resting on an unverified premise.

quantities.name: credit_unit_price_usd
quantities.source: no marginal credit price is recorded for this account anywhere in the repository
quantities.upgrade: One question to the account owner, or one invoice line.

quantities.name: usable_credit_quota
quantities.source: settings.coiled_credit_quota is 400, transcribed from the kill message of 2026-08-22. That is the quota that was hit on one day, not a statement of what this workspace can be granted, and the period boundary is not observable either
quantities.upgrade: Read the workspace usage endpoint, or ask the account owner for the quota and its reset period.

quantities.name: excess_retry_uplift
quantities.source: deliberately small: the reference run already contains a recovery round (offsets_round_2) and a spot reclaim, so the base rate of retrying is inside the anchor and an uplift on top of it would count it twice
quantities.upgrade: Count recovery rounds across a multi-tile calibration run.

quantities.name: contingency
quantities.source: unmodelled all-in slack: driver hours, S3 request charges, a stage re-run after a bug, price drift since pricing.json as_of 2026-08-14
quantities.upgrade: Judgement. Keep it, and keep it named.

quantities.name: approval_ceiling_usd
quantities.source: issue #108 acceptance text; an approval ceiling set by the project owner
quantities.upgrade: Nothing. It is a stated constraint, not an estimate, and it is neither a target nor a prediction.

quantities.name: composite_scaling_basis
quantities.source: scene_counts.json counts STAC items; budgets._scene_count uses solar-day time steps, and the reference run's observed composite matches the solar-day basis within 7% against 3.7x off the item basis. The model scales by a ratio against the same reference, so a constant items-per-group factor cancels exactly
quantities.upgrade: A per-tile solar-day count for all 700 tiles. It is a STAC metadata job, not a compute job, and it removes the largest uncertainty in the term carrying 84% of compute. What does not cancel is the variation: WRS-2 path overlap grows toward the poles, so item-scaling overstates high-latitude tiles. The residual bias is conservative and the model cannot bound it.

quantities.name: reference_vm_hours
quantities.source: sum of every worker's own billed window / 60, from the cluster event logs. The transcribed shape gave 24.55 by charging all 64 workers the wall clock of their cluster; vms x cluster lifetime on the measured lifetimes gives 30.68. Inherits measured.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: reference_vcpu_hours
quantities.source: sum over workers of lifetime x that cluster's vcpus / 60. The transcribed shape gave 317.73, 12 percent higher, because the 16-vCPU composite fleet was the one whose workers exited most unevenly. Inherits measured.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: reference_usd_on_demand
quantities.source: measured worker VM-hours per cluster x the pricing.json list rate. Both inputs are measured, so this one is not weakened by its shape any more.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: implied_spot_factor
quantities.source: 7.28 / 14.71. The denominator is measured and the numerator is not, so this corroborates the AWS anchor against pricing.json's 0.44 sample rather than measuring a spot rate. It sits inside the 0.30-0.75 band either way.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: implied_credits_per_vcpu_hour
quantities.source: 268.1063 / 279.66. Both inputs measured. Against the transcribed shape this read 0.844, which understated the rate by charging vCPU-hours the fleet never billed.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: reference_useful_fraction_of_vm_time
quantities.source: 592 useful VM-min / 1369 total. The denominator is measured and the numerator is not: idle is the residue after boot and compute, so it carries the error in both compute assumptions. offsets_round_1 shows the strain, booking 342 of its 507 VM-minutes as idle because a 6-minute per-unit figure is applied to VMs that lived 34 minutes processing many units.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: total_scenes_700_tiles
quantities.source: sum over results/cost-model/scene_counts.json, a retained artifact of a STAC query. Items, not solar-day groups: see composite_scaling_basis.
quantities.upgrade: A per-tile solar-day count would replace the basis assumption.

quantities.name: mean_land_fraction
quantities.source: mean over results/cost-model/land_fractions.json, computed from Natural Earth 10m buffered 25 km against each 5-degree cell.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: offsets_equivalents
quantities.source: sum(scenes x (land_fraction + 1)) / reference, because phase A skips blocks with no land and phase B reads the full footprint.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: composite_equivalents
quantities.source: sum(scenes) / reference scenes. No land discount: the native stack is read at full footprint whatever the land fraction.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: compute_usd_on_demand
quantities.source: per-stage useful dollars x that stage's equivalents. Work the pipeline must do whatever schedules it, so consolidation cannot touch it.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: provisioning_usd_on_demand
quantities.source: per-stage (boot + idle) dollars x that stage's equivalents. The only layer consolidation acts on.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.

quantities.name: compute_composite_share
quantities.source: composite compute / total compute. After consolidation every further dollar has to come from this pass rather than from scheduling.
quantities.upgrade: Nothing on its own. It inherits the bucket of its weakest input, so it strengthens when that input does.
